capsules.title: Quick facts every :course candidate should know.
capsules.lede: Short facts about eligibility, the exam, and renewal, in one place.

pmp-certification-training.title: 180 questions
pmp-certification-training.text: The PMP exam has 180 questions, with 230 minutes to complete it.

pmp-certification-training.title: Two optional breaks
pmp-certification-training.text: You can take two optional 10-minute breaks during the exam.

pmp-certification-training.title: Three exam domains
pmp-certification-training.text: The exam covers People, Process, and Business Environment.

pmp-certification-training.title: Valid for three years
pmp-certification-training.text: PMP certification is valid for three years and is maintained with 60 PDUs.

pmp-certification-training.title: Two experience paths
pmp-certification-training.text: 36 months of project management experience with a four-year degree, or 60 months with a high school diploma or associate degree.

pmp-certification-training.title: 35 hours of education
pmp-certification-training.text: Candidates need 35 hours of project management education to apply.

pmp-certification-training.title: Exam fee
pmp-certification-training.text: The published exam fee is $405 for PMI members and $555 for non-members.

pmp-certification-training.title: Globally recognized
pmp-certification-training.text: PMP is a globally recognized credential for professionals who want to advance in project management.

pgmp-certification-training.title: No PMP® required
pgmp-certification-training.text: A PMP is not mandatory before PgMP. Applicants must meet PMI program management experience requirements.

pgmp-certification-training.title: Programs, not projects
pgmp-certification-training.text: PgMP focuses on managing multiple related projects as a program. PMP is centered on individual projects.

pgmp-certification-training.title: Five exam domains
pgmp-certification-training.text: Strategic Program Management, Program Lifecycle, Benefits Management, Stakeholder Engagement, and Governance.

pgmp-certification-training.title: Exam fee
pgmp-certification-training.text: The published exam fee is $800 for PMI members and $1,000 for non-members.

pfmp-certification-training.title: 170 MCQ questions
pfmp-certification-training.text: The PfMP exam has 170 multiple-choice questions within a 4-hour window.

pfmp-certification-training.title: Five exam domains
pfmp-certification-training.text: Strategic Alignment, Governance, Portfolio Performance, Portfolio Risk Management, and Communications Management.

pfmp-certification-training.title: 8 + 4 years of experience
pfmp-certification-training.text: A minimum of 8 years of business experience and 4 years of portfolio management experience. Requirements vary by education.

pfmp-certification-training.title: Portfolio over programs
pfmp-certification-training.text: PMP focuses on projects, PgMP on programs, and PfMP on a portfolio aligned to strategy.

pmi-rmp-certification-training.title: 115 MCQ questions
pmi-rmp-certification-training.text: The PMI-RMP exam has 115 multiple-choice questions in 150 minutes.

pmi-rmp-certification-training.title: Five exam domains
pmi-rmp-certification-training.text: Risk Strategy and Planning, Risk Identification, Risk Analysis, Risk Response, and Monitor and Close Risks.

pmi-rmp-certification-training.title: Two eligibility paths
pmi-rmp-certification-training.text: A secondary degree with 36 months of risk experience and 40 hours of risk education, or a four-year degree with 24 months and 30 hours.

pmi-rmp-certification-training.title: Exam fee
pmi-rmp-certification-training.text: The published exam fee is $520 for PMI members and $670 for non-members.

overview.title: Eligibility, audience and value at a glance.

pmp-certification-training.lede: Showcase your capability to lead projects across industries. The PMP® recognizes professionals proficient in managing people, processes, and business objectives in professional project environments.
eligibility: 36 months of project management experience with a four-year degree
Or 60 months of experience with a high school diploma or associate degree
audience: Project managers who want to advance in project management
Professionals leading people, processes, and business objectives
benefits: A globally recognized credential for project managers
Proof of your capability to lead projects across industries
Valid for three years, maintained with 60 PDUs
methodology: PMI Authorized PMP Instructor and PMI approved study material
Application approval assistance and continuous learning support

pgmp-certification-training.lede: A working knowledge of PMI program management practices and preparation for the PgMP® exam, explained with case studies, tools, and templates.
eligibility: A PMP® is not mandatory before PgMP®
Applicants must meet PMI program management experience requirements
Confirm the current requirements in the PMI PgMP Handbook
audience: Leaders of work that spans functions, organisations, clients, and regions
benefits: Recognition for managing multiple related projects as a program
Advanced expertise in coordinated, strategic delivery
Covers Strategic Program Management, Program Lifecycle, Benefits Management, Stakeholder Engagement, and Governance
methodology: Application writing support and personalized learning paths

pfmp-certification-training.lede: Orchestrate the success of project portfolios with precision: balance priorities, watch portfolio performance, and direct resources to where they deliver the greatest impact.
eligibility: A minimum of 8 years of business experience
Requirements vary by education; confirm the current PMI PfMP Handbook
audience: Professionals who manage portfolios of projects and programs
Leaders who align portfolios with organisational strategy
benefits: Direct resources to where they deliver the greatest impact
methodology: Study materials aligned to the latest standard
Covers Strategic Alignment, Governance, Portfolio Performance, Portfolio Risk Management, and Communications Management

pmi-rmp-certification-training.lede: Transform risks into opportunities. The PMI-RMP® equips you to identify issues early, apply core risk principles, and drive better project results.
eligibility: Secondary degree, 36 months of project risk experience in the last 5 years, and 40 hours of risk education
Or a four-year degree, 24 months of experience, and 30 hours of risk education
Confirm the current requirements in the PMI-RMP Handbook
audience: Professionals who specialise in identifying, assessing, and managing project risks
Project professionals who want to spot issues early
benefits: Identify issues early and apply core risk principles
methodology: Study materials aligned to the latest standard
Covers Risk Strategy and Planning, Identification, Analysis, Response, and Monitor and Close Risks
